review_notes: I read the whole file and the FiberBundle class in Mathlib/Topology/FiberBundle/Basic.lean. I checked which hypotheses the fiberwise-trivialization API (continuousLinearMapAt, symmL, continuousLinearEquivAt, apply_eq_prod_continuousLinearEquivAt, Trivialization.zeroSection) actually uses. These declarations sit under the section-wide `variable [NontriviallyNormedField R] ... [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace R F]`. Their proofs use only `Trivialization.continuousOn`, `continuousOn_symm`, `FiberBundle.totalSpaceMk_isInducing` and `continuous_zero`. None of these use norms. The same file already has `coordChangeL`, whose type `F ≃L[R] F` needs no norm, in the weaker `Semiring R` / topological `F` section. I did not compile the generalization. The remaining uncertainty is whether downstream files rely on instance resolution that moving the declarations would change. The `VectorBundle` class itself needs the normed hypotheses, because it states continuity in the operator-norm topology. `continuous_zeroSection` also needs `VectorBundle`, so I did not propose generalizing it. The only generalization I found that is useful and needs no new mathematics is the one in the finding.

findings.problem: These declarations are stated under the section-wide hypotheses `[NontriviallyNormedField R] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace R F]`. Their proofs use none of the norm structure. `continuousLinearMapAt` uses `continuous_if_const`, `continuous_zero`, `Trivialization.continuousOn` and `FiberBundle.totalSpaceMk_isInducing`. `symmL` uses `continuousOn_symm` and `totalSpaceMk_isInducing`. `continuousLinearEquivAt` uses the same facts plus `symmL`. `Trivialization.zeroSection` only uses `map_zero` of the equiv. `FiberBundle` itself only needs `[TopologicalSpace B] [TopologicalSpace F]`, and `E b →L[R] F` only needs `[Semiring R]` with topological module structures. The earlier section of this file already treats `coordChangeL : F ≃L[R] F` under `[Semiring R] [TopologicalSpace F] [TopologicalSpace B]`, so the file is inconsistent about this. The `IsLinear` mixin is likewise stated for a `Semiring`.
findings.proposed_change: Move this block (`continuousLinearMapAt`, `continuousLinearMapAt_apply_of_mem`, `symmL`, `symmL_apply`, `symmL_apply_of_notMem`, `symmL_continuousLinearMapAt`, `continuousLinearMapAt_symmL`, `continuousLinearEquivAt` and its `_eq` / `_apply'` lemmas, `apply_eq_prod_continuousLinearEquivAt`, `Trivialization.zeroSection`) into a section with `[Semiring R] [TopologicalSpace B] [TopologicalSpace F] [AddCommMonoid F] [Module R F] [∀ x, AddCommMonoid (E x)] [∀ x, Module R (E x)] [∀ x, TopologicalSpace (E x)] [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F E)] [FiberBundle F E]`. Keep the proofs unchanged. Leave `continuous_zeroSection` and the other `VectorBundle`-dependent results under the normed hypotheses.
findings.benefit: The trivialization API becomes available for topological vector bundles over arbitrary topological semirings or rings and non-normed fibers, for example locally convex, non-normable or merely topological modules. Today the `IsLinear`/`coordChangeL` API in the first section works there, but these continuous-linear-equivalence lemmas do not. The hypotheses then match what the proofs use, and users no longer have to pull in a `NontriviallyNormedField` just to use `continuousLinearEquivAt`.
